questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to live and study in a very different culture from what I am used to. And as I had previously visited South Korea during a vacation I chose this destination.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Yonsei was very good at explaining everything and we got a lot of mails from the Office of International Affairs with all the information needed.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I arrived quite far in advance before the semester started, so I did not receive any assistance. I do not know whether this is available from Yonsei.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I had heard that it would be easy to find an apartement/accommodation in the city upon arrival, but this was not my experience. Most realtors will not make a contract for only 6 months and the ones that do have quite a high deposit (that you are not sure to get back). I ended up renting a room from a company called Local Stitch. Here you have your own room with a shared kitchen. It is very modern and the people running it are very nice.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you want to find accommodation on your own you should definitely go and visit the places to make sure the apartments and the realtor are legit.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration proces is divided into multiple rounds. In the first round you get 72 points to "bid" on the courses you want. You can see the average of points for the previous years on the course website to get a feeling for how popular the course is. In the second round it is first come, first serve where you can register for courses that are not filled up.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You get a lot of information from the university explaining the whole progress. If you need any information about a specific course you can write to the professors.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have multiple plans for what courses you want to take as you a not guaranteed any place. Make sure the classes do not overlap, as attendance is part of the grade - so you have to show up to the classes.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the different courses varied a lot. Some of my courses were of the same difficulty as I would expect at Copenhagen and some were easier.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is very different. There are only lectures and no class hours where you go though the material. Also as you are taking 5 different courses at the same time, the courses were more superficial than the courses in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Genetic analysis
Virus and host
Biotechnology in Diagnostics 
Cancer biology
Basic Korean III

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Cancer biology was really good. It is not officially open for exchange students, but the professor let me take the course anyway. I would also recommend taking a Korean course, just to be able to know the basics in Korean.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to pay for the national health insurance (you can try to get an exemption). You also have to pay a one time fee for the ARC application.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Restaurants are very cheap to eat at. Transportation is very cheap also. But fruit is very expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There is a really nice buddy programme, where you are paired with a local student and a group of international students. This is a really nice way to meet new people. They also plan activities for all the buddies to do together. 
I also started doing Taekwondo for international students, which was really fun! I also participated in some language exchange programmes. But a lot of the social clubs are not open for international students, unless you are fluent in Korean.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the buddy programme, as it is a really good way to meet new people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Seoul is so big that there is always something to do in the city! But doing weekend or day trips is really nice as well. I would definitely suggest going to Busan and Jeju. Nami Island is also really beautiful.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I would say it is quite easy. Everyone is very welcoming and willing to answer questions if you have any.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Sometimes the large language barrier is a bit challenging to navigate.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Seoul is such a vibrant city and there is always something to do. In addition the country is very safe, so you never feel uneasy walking anywhere.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Start with all the practical things as soon as you can, this especially includes applying for the ARC. I arrived and applied very early, but still only received my card in October as there is a massive rush in the applications at the start of the semester. 
Just experience everything you can while you are away!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not that I can think of right now.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting a lot of new people and experiencing such a different culture together. The university culture in Korea is also very different from the Danish, with games between the universities (that of course are very important to win;))

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The language barrier is always difficult to navigate, but it always works out anyways.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
